edit.description: the membership read that already settles such a tag silently
the leg that carries its post-selection facts onto the result
the reported facts a handoff may refuse on

summary: selection reports a blocker tag no queue entry carries on `TickResult.unresolvedBlockers`, so a misspelled blocker is visible rather than a silently open gate
acceptance: a queue whose `blockedBy` names a tag no entry carries reports that tag on `TickResult.unresolvedBlockers` under both concurrencies, and the entry stays pickable
tests: a blockedBy naming a tag no queue entry carries is reported as an unresolved blocker
a singleton tick's result carries the unresolved blockers its selection found
a fanout tick's result carries the unresolved blockers its selection found
pins: an entry whose blockedBy names a tag no queue entry carries stays pickable

interface.changes: `TickResult.unresolvedBlockers` names the blocker tags this tick's selection found no queue entry for; a chain's handoff or refusal may read it
interface.hides: the membership read itself — absence from the queue is how a ship reads, and a chain never re-walks the listing to tell a landed blocker from a misspelt one
interface.rejected: refusing such a tag at the queue parse, which would make a restored or relocated queue unrunnable — the engine reports the fact and the chain decides (`.claude/rules/engine-boundary.md`, *Routing rule*)

notes: `settledBlockers` (`src/selection.ts`) already counts absence from the queue as landed, which is the section's other half and needs nothing; what no surface reports is *which* tags that was. Not a hold: the entry is pickable, so `PickableSelection`'s hold count stands at three.
